editorial:
Imagine growing up in a huge house full of expensive things but feeling like you have no real connection to the people around you. You will meet Raphaela, a blind teenager whose parents are completely falling apart. Her dad is checked out and cheating with his secretary just to avoid his problems at home. Meanwhile, her mom is so worried and scared that she becomes way too controlling, treating Raphaela more like a possession than a person. The whole vibe is heavy and tense, making you feel the pressure of a family that has all the money in the world but zero happiness.

What really hits home is the acting, as you can feel the frustration boiling over in every scene. The pacing is a bit slow, which might bug some of you, but it helps you feel how trapped these characters are. If you enjoy deep family dramas that don't sugarcoat the truth, you should definitely give this a shot. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a remastered 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture quality, or see if you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: The story wraps up when the tension finally breaks and the family's secrets come to light. Raphaela begins to push back against her mother's controlling nature, seeking her own independence. The miracle mentioned in the title is more about an emotional awakening than a physical cure. By the end, the family has to face their lies and mistakes, leaving you to wonder if they can actually heal or if the damage is too deep.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional stories about broken families.
